title: Sunday habits
hookLine: a regular seat, arriving early, staying after
tomorrow: who are all those people at Mass who aren't the priest?

cards: Late again: the parking lot, the back pew, the opening song already going, and out the door before the last verse ends. Mass can turn into something squeezed between other things.
But the few minutes on either side of the hour are where a parish meets itself: who kneels early, who's sitting alone, who lingers by the door.

teach.b: The letter to the Hebrews treats the gathering itself as something you can drift from: "Not forsaking our assembly, as some are accustomed; but comforting one another."
The Catechism quotes that verse when it speaks of Sunday, and says the Christian assembly goes back to the time of the apostles. So, three small habits.
A regular seat: people learn your face, you learn theirs, and you notice who's missing.
Arriving early: a few minutes to kneel, to read the readings, to greet whoever's beside you.
Staying after: the coffee, the hallway, the parking lot, where the gathering keeps going.
Luke says the first believers in Jerusalem met day after day and broke bread in their homes with gladness; the meal after the meeting is an old habit. Each one is this week in miniature.
Decide first, before you feel like going. Go first, with a hello. Keep an open table.
Notice who's alone in the pew. Stay with someone who's grieving. And let yourself be loved by people who are glad you came.

how: Catholics gather for Mass on Sunday or the evening before; some parishes host coffee or a meal afterward, and some people come a few minutes early to pray.

s: the Christian Sunday gathering began long after the apostles
the Catechism says the Christian assembly goes back to the time of the apostles.
Jesus wept at Lazarus's tomb because he had lost hope
he wept because the people he loved were weeping.
in Matthew 5, the brother is the one holding the grudge
thy brother hath any thing against thee, and you're the one who goes first.

games.q: you arrive early on Sunday and notice an older man alone a few rows up, in the seat where his wife always sat. what fits this week?
o: sit near him, say hello, and stay after to talk.
leave him be; Mass is a private time with God.
mention it to the priest so someone else can check in.
games.why: that's the week in one move: go first, not alone in it, just stay. early and staying make the room for it.

practice: Stand and walk slowly, the way you'd walk up an aisle to a seat that's been yours for years. With each step, let one face from this week come to mind, someone you'd hope to see on Sunday.
When you stop, stay standing a moment, as if you'd arrived early. If you pray, you can pray for the people you'd sit beside.

wordCard.voice: Sunday habits. The small, steady ways of showing up for the Sunday gathering: a regular seat, an early arrival, and staying after. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: of the Lord, from dies Dominica, the Lord's day: the Church's old name for Sunday.

carryVoice: Keep this one: early and staying, a few minutes on each side of the hour. That's the week.
